quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Do not drive if you feel tired.
Check that your headlights work properly.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. Take steps to protect yourself and other drivers on the road.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is just as dangerous as driving while drunk. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: What affects how long it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
How good your brakes and tires are.
What condition the road is in.

questions.explanation: Your stopping distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?

options.text: The medicine reduces the alcohol's effect.
The alcohol helps the medicine cure a cold.
The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
There is no effect because they are different.

questions.correctAnswerText: The combination can increase the effects of both the alcohol and medicine.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with other medicines can make both stronger and more dangerous. For example, one drink with a cold medicine might affect you like several drinks would on their own.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
Signal only if other cars are nearby.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if no other cars are nearby.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from the curb. Do not skip signaling because you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers are buckled up.
Make sure only adults are buckled up.
Make sure only children are buckled up.
Make sure everyone in the car is buckled up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car is buckled up.
questions.explanation: Before you start driving, buckle your seat belt and make sure all your passengers do the same.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot enter this road or driveway from your current direction. If you see this sign, turn around and find another route.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car, every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car, every time.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt at all times. Without a seat belt, a person can become a projectile and hurt others in a crash.

questions.question: When you see a stopped school bus with red warning lights on, you:

options.text: Cannot pass it. It is against the law.
Only need to stop if you see children.
Do not need to stop if you are in a school yard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot pass it. It is against the law.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to pass a stopped school bus with red warning lights on, even in a school yard. The only exception is if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road.
Driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end collisions happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show them they are wrong.
Do something to get back at the aggressive driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Trying to get revenge can make things worse and more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medicines (prescription and over-the-counter).

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic laws as if the area was not under construction.

questions.explanation: You must slow down and follow signs, flaggers, or police officers directing traffic in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces the skills you need to drive safely. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving while impaired is a serious safety problem. You cannot drive safely after drinking alcohol or using drugs. Impaired driving endangers you and others on the road.

questions.question: Which statement about bicyclists is true?

options.text: They have a legal right to ride on most roads.
They have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers.
They must use hand signals before turning.

questions.explanation: Bicyclists can legally ride on most roads except interstate highways. They must follow the same traffic rules as vehicles. When turning, they must use proper hand signals.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic is merging from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is merging from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is merging into your lane from the right.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, when there is a stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, you should:
questions.explanation: When you see railroad crossing signs, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Do not go around the gate.
